name: McDonald's
oneLiner: The largest fast-food chain on earth, and the one whose figures are easiest to check and hardest to hold in your head.
longIntro: McDonald's publishes its nutrition information, because in most of the markets it trades in the law requires that. What it does not do is make it easy to compare: the figures live inside a calculator that shows one item at a time, per portion only, with percentages measured against a daily allowance that belongs to nobody in particular. This page holds what that calculator says, item by item, with the date a person read it. Where we hold more than one country for the same product, both are shown, because the same product is formulated differently in each and the numbers move with it. That is also where the calculators themselves start to differ: the Canadian one gives the weight of a portion in grams and the American one does not, which is the difference between a figure you can compare and a figure you have to take on trust.
